sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by FACS in 293T cells; TGFβ1 activation function not explicitly assayed for the FLAG-tagged construct alone in these clips.
sites.rationale: The ledger (L1–L4) reports a FLAG tag placed at the N-terminus of full-length LRRC32. The signal peptide spans residues 1–19 (last SP residue = Q19); a tag upstream of the mature protein must be inserted after residue 19 to survive SP cleavage and reach the cell surface, which is confirmed by FACS detection of surface FLAG-GARP. There is exactly one extracellular N-terminus (residue 20, H), so the junction is topology-derived at insert_after_residue = 19. Python verification confirms seq[18]='Q' and seq[19]='H', consistent with the landmarks. Full-length human GARP (LRRC32) was subcloned into a modified pLEXm vector with a FLAG tag at the N-terminus (L1). The construct was expressed in 293T cells and surface FLAG-GARP was detected by FACS (L2, L3, L4), confirming cell-surface display of the N-terminally FLAG-tagged full-length protein.

sources.claim: GARP was subcloned into a modified pLEXm vector ( Aricescu et al. , 2006 ) with a FLAG tag at the N-terminus.

literature_notes: L5–L7 (PMC3127830) describe GFP fused to either the N- or C-terminus of full-length LRRC32. The N-terminal GFP construct (N-GFP/LRRC32) places GFP before the signal peptide; L7 shows the resulting 31 kDa band (GFP + ~2 kDa LRRC32 fragment) is consistent with SP cleavage removing the GFP, so this is NOT a surface tag and is not proposed as a site. The C-terminal GFP construct (C-GFP/LRRC32) places GFP after residue 662, which is intracellular (topology: 649–662 = intracellular); this is recorded in other_positions. L8 (PMC9472209) describes HA-tagged chimeric human/murine GARP constructs but does not state the position of the HA tag insertion; it cannot be pinned to a residue or junction and is therefore not proposed as a site.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusion (C-GFP/LRRC32) places GFP after the last residue (A662), which is intracellular (topology 649–662); not a surface tag site.
